requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was created as UID/GID 1001 with /home/appworker and /bin/bash, and its continued existence was directly observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: Persistent soft and hard nofile=8192 and nproc=256 entries were installed. Actual appworker SSH login sessions directly showed all four effective values before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were observed before and after execution. The implementation used existing legacy-compatible account, PAM limits, shell, and SSH facilities without package or platform replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart observations. The provider-wide restart protocol substantially demonstrates baseline function, acknowledged restart, bounded unavailability, a changed boot identity, and recovery of the account, configuration, and effective login limits.
limitations: The restart acknowledgement in cmd-090cb258993c4cc7 printed an empty pre_boot_id because of command construction, although the immediately preceding baseline and fixed lifecycle snapshots coherently establish the old boot identity and the post-restart identity differs.

Failed-service collection was unsupported on this pre-systemd platform, so recovery confidence relies on successful SSH command execution and direct account/limits checks rather than a service-manager health inventory.
The retained limits.conf backup was not explicitly listed in final evidence; its continued presence is inferred from its successful creation and the absence of any later removal command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were tightly related to account creation, limits configuration, required restart evidence, or bounded SSH-session verification, and temporary credentials were removed. One unnecessary retained residue was identified: cmd-9837fa07ce5448cf created /etc/security/limits.conf.pre-appworker as a precautionary backup, but no later command removed it or used it in the final solution. The temporary SSH keys, authorized_keys, and known-hosts material were fully removed by cmd-652c21557d9b455b. Lifecycle checks found no /tmp residue or package-health regression after execution.
